the contribution of ryanodines receptor type 3 to the expression of contextual fear conditioning behavior.
the contribution of ryanodines receptor type 3 to learning and memory.
the relationship between contextual learning behavior, Ca(2+)/ calmodulin-dependent protein kinases II and ryanodine receptors.

the ryanodine receptors type 1, 2, and 3, and the inositol 1, 4, 5-trisphosphate receptors, are all important to the learning and memory processes.

the ryanodine receptors play a critical role in the expression of the contextual learning and the fear response.
